translation_en: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Hujayn informed us: al-Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, who informed him that Fatimah daughter of the Messenger of Allah sent to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq asking him for her inheritance from the Messenger of Allah, from what Allah had granted him at Madinah, Fadak, and what remained of the fifth from Khaybar. Abu Bakr said: The Messenger of Allah said: We are not inherited; what we leave is charity. The family of Muhammad only eats from this property. By Allah, I will not change anything of the charity of the Messenger of Allah from the condition it was in during the Messenger of Allah's time, and I will act concerning it as the Messenger of Allah acted. Abu Bakr refused to give Fatimah anything from it. Fatimah was upset with Abu Bakr about this and stopped speaking to him until she died. She lived six months after the Messenger of Allah. When she died, her husband 'Ali ibn Abi Talib buried her at night without informing Abu Bakr, and 'Ali prayed over her. During Fatimah's lifetime, 'Ali had standing among the people. When she died, 'Ali found the people's attitude changed, so he sought reconciliation with Abu Bakr and to pledge allegiance to him; he had not pledged allegiance during those months. He sent word to Abu Bakr: Come to us, and do not bring anyone with you, because he disliked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab's presence. 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: By Allah, do not go to them alone. Abu Bakr said: What could they do to me? By Allah, I will go to them. Abu Bakr entered upon them. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib began by bearing witness, then said: Abu Bakr, we recognize your virtue and what Allah has given you. We do not envy you for any good that Allah has brought to you. But you took this authority for yourself instead of consulting us, while we believed we had a right to it because of our kinship with the Messenger of Allah. He continued speaking to Abu Bakr until Abu Bakr's eyes overflowed with tears. When Abu Bakr spoke, he said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, maintaining the kinship of the Messenger of Allah is dearer to me than maintaining my own kinship. As for the disagreement between us concerning these properties, I have not failed to pursue what is right, and I have not abandoned anything I saw the Messenger of Allah do concerning them without doing the same. 'Ali said to Abu Bakr: Your appointment with me is this evening for the pledge. After Abu Bakr prayed the noon prayer, he ascended the pulpit, bore witness, and spoke about 'Ali and his delay in pledging allegiance, and the explanation he had given him. Then he sought forgiveness and bore witness. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib then bore witness and affirmed Abu Bakr's right, saying that what he had done was not motivated by envy of Abu Bakr or denial of the virtue Allah had given him. Rather, we believed we had a share in this matter, but it was taken from us without consultation, and we were distressed. The Muslims were pleased by this, and said: You have done well. After 'Ali returned to the recognized course of affairs, the Muslims were close to him.
